record.paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
record.original_question: Why do heavy-tailed Weibull inter-arrival and service distributions appear to follow the same GI/G/1/K BRAVO behavior predicted by Conjecture 1, while Lognormal and Pareto distributions with the same first two moments appear to show a different asymptotic departure-variance behavior? More concretely, what mathematical property separates the distributions that converge to the conjectured factor 1/3 from those that appear to converge to a different limit or to converge much more slowly?

evidence.quote: The figure indicates that Lognormal and Pareto distributions exhibit one type of behavior (having a BRAVO effect but possibly not with a factor of 1/3) and in contrast the heavy-tailed Weibull exhibits behaviors similar to light-tailed distributions as in Conjecture 1.
Open Problem Heavy-tailed Weibull and light-tailed distributions exhibit one type of behavior, in agreement with Conjecture 1. Lognormal and Pareto exhibit a different behavior.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with a finite buffer of size $K$ (a GI/G/1/K queue): customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. inter-arrival times having distribution $A$ (mean $1/\lambda$, squared coefficient of variation $c_a^2$), are served by a single server with i.i.d. service times having distribution $S$ (mean $1/\mu$, squared coefficient of variation $c_s^2$), and any customer arriving to a full buffer is lost. Operate the queue in the critically loaded regime $\lambda=\mu$, and let $D(t)$ denote the number of customer departures in $[0,t]$ in steady state. Define the asymptotic variance rate
$$ V_K := \lim_{t\to\infty} \frac{\operatorname{Var}(D(t))}{t}, $$
and the BRAVO factor
$$ B_K := \frac{V_K}{\lambda\,(c_a^2+c_s^2)}. $$
It is conjectured that for "nice" inter-arrival and service distributions, $B_K \to 1/3$ as $K\to\infty$ (the GI/G/1/K BRAVO conjecture).

Numerical experiments suggest the following dichotomy when $A$ and $S$ are chosen from heavy-tailed families with matched first two moments:
(i) If $A$ and $S$ are heavy-tailed Weibull distributions (shape parameter $<1$), then $B_K$ appears to converge to $1/3$, behaving like light-tailed distributions.
(ii) If $A$ and $S$ are Lognormal or Pareto distributions with the same mean and variance, $B_K$ appears to converge to a different limit, or to converge to $1/3$ extremely slowly.

Problem. Prove or disprove the conjecture $B_K\to 1/3$ for heavy-tailed Weibull inter-arrival and service distributions, and identify a precise distributional property (for example, a tail-decay condition, a moment/Laplace-transform criterion, or a subexponentiality-type characterization) that separates those inter-arrival/service distributions for which $B_K\to 1/3$ holds from those for which it fails or converges at a strictly slower rate. In particular, explain mathematically why heavy-tailed Weibull distributions belong to the former class while Lognormal and Pareto distributions (with the same first two moments) belong to the latter.
artifact.status_search_result: The GI/G/1/K BRAVO conjecture (factor 1/3) remains an open problem. Recent works on critically loaded queues and generalized BRAVO (e.g., on busy periods of the critical GI/G/1 queue and BRAVO, and oscillating cumulants/generalized BRAVO) extend related results, but do not provide a distributional criterion explaining the observed heavy-tailed Weibull vs. Lognormal/Pareto dichotomy. No source confirms a proof of the GI/G/1/K conjecture or characterization separating the two regimes.

status_evidence.title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Article presenting the GI/G/1/K BRAVO conjecture and its observed failure for Lognormal/Pareto.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open problem in the queueing literature.

status_evidence.title: Phase transitions and departure statistics of critically loaded queues: oscillating cumulants and generalized BRAVO
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work generalizing BRAVO; does not resolve the heavy-tailed Weibull vs. Lognormal/Pareto dichotomy.
status_evidence.claim: Newer literature extends BRAVO but does not resolve the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On busy periods of the critical GI/G/1 queue and BRAVO
status_evidence.snippet: Studies BRAVO via busy periods in the critical GI/G/1 setting.
status_evidence.claim: Related progress on BRAVO but not for finite-buffer GI/G/1/K under heavy-tailed regimes.
